content:
customer-support: FYI escalation from Acct team — customer reports our quantized endpoint (INT8) is both slower and worse quality than their FP16 variant. They attached a small repro payload and latency numbers. They've asked for urgent mitigation.

alex: :eyes: Can you paste the repro (curl) and the exact latency numbers they measured? Also the model name + endpoint config (quant profile).

customer-support: Here are the details they sent:
- Endpoint: /v1/serve/reddemo-gpt2-quant (model: reddemo/gpt-2-like, variant: int8-autocalib)
- Sample prompt: "Summarize the following: <long article>" (avg input tokens 240)
- Observed: 340ms/token (INT8) vs 120ms/token (FP16) on same customer traffic shape. Quality: hallucinations / weird tokenization errors ~5% more.
- Repro curl (sanitized):
```bash
curl -s -H \"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -d '{"model":"reddemo/gpt-2-like","variant":"int8-autocalib","input":"<long article>","max_tokens":512}'
```

maya: Thanks — running a local repro now. Quick note: when I ran that with our internal load generator I see latency 3x for long contexts only; short prompts (<=32 tokens) are fine. Suspect KV cache interaction or kernel fallback.

sandeep: I pulled a trace from a repro run and here's the runtime kernel selection output (snippet):
```
[2025-10-18T14:10:12.345Z] kernel_dispatch: chosen=int8_fused_attention_fast hw=ampere seq_len=256 head=32
[2025-10-18T14:10:12.346Z] kernel_dispatch: chosen=int8_generic_attention_ref (fallback) reason=unsupported_seq_len(240-512)
[2025-10-18T14:10:12.347Z] kv_cache: requantizing KV tensors -> extra memcpy + dequant
[2025-10-18T14:10:12.420Z] step_time: 0.34s (int8 ref)
```
This shows dispatch choosing an optimized int8 kernel for some shapes then immediately falling back to the slow generic ref kernel for the actual sequence length the customer uses. The fallback path is CPU/memory heavy.

julia: Also note calibration flags: the endpoint was configured `int8-autocalib` which runs a lightweight on-the-fly scale adapt. For long contexts that interacts badly with our continuous-batching heuristic and prefix caching — we end up re-calibrating and reconverting cached KV per request which is expensive.

alex: So root causes likely: 1) kernel dispatch table doesn't cover the customer's seq_len/head config so we fallback to slow kernel; 2) autocalibration + KV cache triggers frequent re-quantize/transpose ops; 3) batching heuristics produce many small batches causing overhead.

sandeep: Agreed. Quick mitigation options (ranked by low-friction):
- Immediate rollback: point customer to the FP16 variant (config change on their endpoint) — fastest fix.
- Force FP16 kernels on that INT8 endpoint (`runtime.force_fp16_kernels=true`) to avoid slow INT8 fallback path while preserving smaller memory footprint from fp16.
- Disable KV cache for long-context generation temporarily (`cache_mode=off`) so we avoid repeated re-quantization of cached tensors (tradeoff: higher token compute).
- Re-deploy a calibrated INT8 profile for their exact seq_len/head config (take ~2-4h) — longer but restores cost benefit.

maya: I ran quick experiments: with `runtime.force_fp16_kernels=true` the 340ms/token -> 130ms/token (close to FP16). Disabling KV cache reduced variance but increased total GPU flops about 10%. Recalibrated int8 that matches seq_len=240 yields 140ms/token but gen quality improved back to baseline.

customer-support: CS informed customer of the FP16 rollback option and offered the temporary setting change. They prefer automated fix rather than manual rollback.

alex: Proposed action items:
1) Ops: apply `force_fp16_kernels` to customer's endpoint as a short-term patch. (ops-bot, please create a canary change for their region).
2) Runtime: add missing kernel dispatch entries for seq_len range 240-512 and add a fast path for KV-compatible shapes (sandeep/maya) — targeted PR by EOD.
3) Product/CS: offer to run a per-customer calibration job to produce a calibrated INT8 artifact and re-deploy (julia + customer-support).
4) Devex/Docs: add guidance about `int8-autocalib` caveats for long-context flows.

ops-bot: Created ticket INF-4821 and canary rollout scheduled to region us-west-2 at 2025-10-18T18:00Z. Link: https://issues.redwood.ai/INF-4821

sandeep: Quick perf patch plan: PR will (a) add dispatch table entries for seq_len 240/256/320/384/512, (b) avoid memcopy by keeping quantized KV layout stable across steps when autocalib is enabled, (c) add stats delta logging to surface fallback rates. I have a local branch `int8-dispatch-kvpersist` — testing now.

julia: Comms: send an update to customer that we can either flip them to FP16 instantly or run a calibration that will restore INT8 performance within a few hours. We should apologize, give ETA, and avoid promising cost savings until calib verifies.

alex: I'll coordinate the canary and get a status update in ~2h. For now CS can offer the FP16 rollback that customer can accept.

customer-support: Customer acknowledged and prefer we run customer-specific calibration first. They've shared a larger sample corpus (S3 link). CS will upload to our calibration pipeline.

maya: Received corpus, kicking off calibration run. If successful we push calibrated-int8 -> canary in ~3h and monitor fallback rates + token latencies.

alex: Thanks team. Please post any profiler snippets here. I'll update execs if canary confirms perf recovery. :thumbsup:
